Job Description

Duration: 5 years

Salary: £27,400

Location: Bristol

Start: September 2027

Qualifications: Study for a level 4 Actuarial Technician followed by a degree level programme. Training and costs will be taken care of.

Predict the future. And protect it
Love maths and critical thinking? Step this way.

Make sure our insurance decision makers have all the facts and stats they need. Help us keep on the right track while protecting 28 million customers.

Actuaries don’t have crystal balls. But they do have sharp brains, serious maths skills and the tech to see around corners. They’re the people who spot what’s coming - from how long people might live, how often accidents might happen, to how markets may behave and shift.

They make sure the financial promises we make today still stand decades from now.

And if you join us as an Actuarial apprentice, you won’t just watch it happen. You’ll be in the mix, shaping the big calls sooner than you think.

Your all‑access pass to Actuarial
This is your pass to experience one of the most influential careers in Finance.

You’ll rotate through different teams, spending about 18 months in each. Each placement gives you the chance to build hands-on experience and see just how broad and impactful actuarial work can be.

You could be:

  • Pricing insurance, pensions and investments using specialist techniques to make sure we’re fair and competitive.
  • Calculating reserves and capital so we can pay out future claims when our customers need us most.
  • Using actuarial and statistical modelling techniques to understand and prepare for a wide range of risks.
  • Designing and developing actuarial models and software to predict outcomes and guide decisions.
  • Analysing past data and trends to set smart assumptions that power our models.
  • Optimising investment strategies to keep us aligned with regulatory requirements and risk appetite.
  • Explaining complex concepts to stakeholders and presenting financial results that influence strategic thinking.

And yes, sometimes it’ll be your job to translate all that into plain English for colleagues and leaders. (Because not everyone speaks fluent “actuarial.” Yet.)

Skills for now. Skills for life
You’ll nail how to create, verify and review accurate, timely financial information while working with the latest and greatest tools and tech: Excel/VBA, Python, R, Prophet and Power BI.

Along the way, you’ll level up your maths, problem-solving, data storytelling and communication skills. And get the confidence to explain complex ideas simply (which is super useful for any career).

We’re modernising how we work, too. Creating a more agile, automated and insight-driven environment. You’ll be part of that transformation, helping us improve how we use data and models across the business.

And because we believe talent belongs in the spotlight, you’ll have plenty of chances to show what you can do. Whether that’s finding a smarter way to run a model or presenting your insight to the people making the big decisions.

Your future, fully funded
You’ll start earning a good salary from the moment you join, while working towards the level 4 Actuarial Technician apprenticeship.

From there, you’ll move on to a degree-level programme with the Institute and Faculty of Actuaries (IFoA) - and could go all the way to Fellowship status, with high earning potential and strong long-term career prospects.

Your training - fully funded with a generous study package: study days, tutorials, materials, exams and professional subscriptions - the whole kit and kaboodle.

Plus, you’ll be backed by mentors, local education leads and a close-knit actuarial community that’s ready to help you smash it.

By the end, you won’t just understand actuarial work. You’ll have the skills, qualifications and confidence to make a career-defining impact. And you’ll have played a vital role in Helping Britain Prosper.

Requirements

What you’ll need

  • You’ll need to be at least 18 years old on 1st September 2027
  • GCSE at grade 4-9 in both Maths and English (achieved)
  • You’ll need a minimum of 104 UCAS Tariff points, including a B in A-level Maths (these grades can be predicted, but any offer made to you will be conditional upon successful achievement of these qualifications)

If you’re unsure of your UCAS points, you can visit to check your total.

These grades can be predicted, but any offer made to you will be conditional upon successful achievement of these qualifications

Important information

An additional requirement for the apprenticeship position is that you must currently possess a valid Right to Work in the UK. Your visa end date must extend beyond the duration of the apprenticeship programme, which will last up to five years.

Due to Home Office requirements regarding Skilled Workers, we’re unable to accept applications for visa sponsorship for our apprenticeship roles as the proposed salary for the role does not meet the minimum threshold – if this situation applies to you, please consider looking for other vacancies which may be more suitable.

Location

This apprenticeship is based in Bristol, and you will be expected to work from the Bristol office throughout the programme. While our hybrid working policy requires office attendance at least two days per week (40% for full-time colleagues), apprentices are expected to be in the office most days during the initial settling-in period.

If your commute exceeds 1.5 hours, we strongly recommend relocating closer to the office to ensure consistent attendance in line with contractual and hybrid working expectations.

About working for us
Our ambition is to be the leading UK business for diversity, equity and inclusion supporting our customers, colleagues and communities and we’re committed to creating an environment in which everyone can thrive, learn and develop.

We were one of the first major organisations to set goals on diversity in senior roles, create a menopause health package, and a dedicated Working with Cancer Initiative.

We offer reasonable workplace adjustments for colleagues with disabilities, including flexibility in office attendance, location and working patterns. And, as a Disability Confident Leader, we guarantee interviews for a fair and proportionate number of applicants who meet the minimum criteria for the role with a disability, long-term health or neurodivergent condition through the Disability Confident Scheme.

We provide reasonable adjustments throughout the recruitment process to reduce or remove barriers. Just let us know what you need.

Salary

You will join us on a fixed apprenticeship salary. Upon successful completion of the apprenticeship, you will be re-graded, with your pay range consistent with the job family for your business area.

We also offer a wide-ranging benefits package, which includes:

  • A generous pension contribution of up to 15%
  • An annual performance-related bonus
  • Share schemes including free shares
  • Benefits you can adapt to your lifestyle, such as discounted shopping
  • 22 days’ holiday, with bank holidays on top
  • A range of wellbeing initiatives and generous parental leave policies

The closing date to apply for this opportunity is 12th January 2027

Our roles generate a lot of interest and occasionally we need to close for applications earlier than originally advertised. If you think working with us could be right for you, please apply now and see where an apprenticeship with us can take you!

If you have any queries regarding the recruitment process, please email lloydsbankinggroup@cappfinity.com and a member of our team will be happy to help and will reply within 3 working days (Monday – Friday).


What happens next?
Submit your application → Complete the online assessments → If successful, attend the Assessment Centre in March → Receive your outcome.

At Lloyds Banking Group, we're driven by a clear purpose; to help Britain prosper. Across the Group, our colleagues are focused on making a difference to customers, businesses and communities. With us you'll have a key role to play in shaping the financial services of the future, whilst the scale and reach of our Group means you'll have many opportunities to learn, grow and develop.

We're focused on creating a values-led culture and are committed to building a workforce which reflects the diversity of the customers and communities we serve. Together we’re building a truly inclusive workplace where all of our colleagues have the opportunity to make a real difference.

title: Retail Store Management - New Store
description:
Position Overview

If you are interested in growing your retail management career with one of the largest and fastest growing off-price retailers in the nation, join the Burlington Stores team as a Store Manager! Are you a proven leader with strong communication and organization skills? Can you lead a team in driving results while building strong teams and partnerships and cultivating an environment based on trust, respect, and integrity? Can you bring innovative ideas to help drive results as you take on the challenge of running all aspects of a multi-million-dollar store operation? If you answer yes, then this may be the right opportunity for you.

As a Store Manager, you’ll be responsible for successfully managing all store operations tasks to maximize sales results while bringing “Our Burlington” values to life in your store. You will be a mentor, role model, and coach for your team members, as well as a partner to associates in other branches of the organization. You will lead your team by example, demonstrating how to deliver excellent customer service with a high degree of professionalism and provide a world-class shopping experience to customers. You will take ownership for the successful execution of all day-to-day merchandising, operations and service management tasks. You are ultimately responsible for the overall success of your store location and the associates on your team.

A Day in the Life

  • Direct management and oversight of Assistant Managers, Supervisors, and Store Associates to ensure implementation of established company policies, standards, expectations and initiatives.
  • Ensure Assistant Managers and store team members are fulfilling their individual responsibilities.
  • Partner with Assistant Store Manager, Merchandising to coordinate merchandise placement, sales promotions and pricing.
  • Partner with Assistant Store Manager, Operations to review receiving, transfers, debits/damages, returns-to-vendor (RTV's), and chargeback paperwork to ensure accuracy of inventory.
  • Act as Manager on Duty (MOD); lead by example, set the standard, and create a strong leadership presence by following and modeling the Burlington SOPs.
  • Manage multi-million-dollar sales volume and expense budget including review of all associated reporting and record-keeping.
  • Recruitment, screening and hiring of associates in order to meet store staffing needs.
  • Facilitate onboarding and training for new associates, provide ongoing coaching in the moment, and implement structured learning and development activities for all team members.
  • Handle personnel and associate relations issues.
  • Payroll budget management, workforce management and scheduling.
  • Facilitate effective communication and partnerships among the store team, district and regional management teams, and other partners within the company.

You'll Come With

  • 5+ years of Retail Management experience in a Big Box or Specialty environment
  • Must be able to work a flexible schedule; including early mornings, nights, weekends, and holidays as required.
  • Ability to lift and move boxes weighing up to 40 lbs.
  • Experience utilizing scheduling and reporting computer software
  • Travel may be required from time to time.

Pay Range

  • Store Manager: $74,420 - $93,025 / annual
  • Operations/Service Manager: $23.20 - $30.95 / hour

Come join our team. You’re going to like it here!

You will enjoy a competitive wage, flexible hours, and an associate discount. Burlington’s benefits package includes medical, dental and vision coverage including life and disability insurance. Full time associates may also be eligible for up to 12 days of paid time off annually, up to 8 paid holidays, paid sick time in accordance with applicable law, and a 401(k) plan. We are a rapidly growing brand and provide a variety of training and development opportunities so our associates can grow with us.

Our store teams work hard and have fun together! Burlington associates make a difference in the lives of customers, colleagues, and the communities where we live and work every day. Burlington Stores, Inc. is an equal opportunity employer committed to workplace diversity.

Individual pay decisions will be based on a variety of factors, such as but not limited to, qualifications, education, job-related skills, relevant experience, and geographic location.

title: AI Director - Addovation
description:
Do you want to shape how AI creates value for customers, colleagues and businesses? At Addovation, AI is already part of our everyday work in delivery, support, sales and in the solutions we build for our customers. We're now looking for a AI Director who wants to take our AI journey to the next level and play a key role in driving business impact and innovations. With a clear mandate from the leadership team and sponsorship across the business, you will have the opportunity to turn AI ambitions into measurable business outcomes.

About the role

AI is transforming the way businesses operate, and at Addovation we see tremendous opportunities to help both our customers and our own organization benefit from that change.

As AI Director, you will lead the direction of AI across Addovation. You will be responsible for identifying opportunities, turning ideas into scalable solutions, and ensuring AI becomes a natural part of the way we work and deliver value. This is a strategic role with a strong operational element, where you will collaborate closely with business leaders, consultants, developers and customers across the organization.

You will lead Addovation's AI Council, bringing together stakeholders from across the organization to align priorities, accelerate adoption and ensure business value.

You will have the opportunity to influence both our initial AI adaption and the AI-powered services we bring to the market.

What you'll do

As AI Director, you will:

- Define and drive Addovation’s AI strategy, roadmap and priorities.

- Define the direction for AI platforms, data foundations and AI agent architectures, ensuring solutions can be deployed securely and at scale.

- Drive an AI-first way of working across delivery, sales and operations, helping teams embed AI naturally into daily work while taking advantage of “old school” competencies and capabilities where suitable.

- Work closely with business units to develop AI-powered offerings and services within areas such as IFS, NetSuite, Oracle and Microsoft technologies.

- Lead and coordinate AI initiatives across functions, ensuring business goals and technology capabilities align.

- Drive AI adoption internally by enabling teams with tools, knowledge and best practices.

- Establish governance, security and compliance frameworks for responsible AI usage.

- Collaborate with IT and security teams to ensure AI solutions meet regulatory and organizational requirements.

- Build and lead a network of AI Ambassadors who support adoption, knowledge sharing and experimentation throughout the organisation.

- Represent Addovation externally in customer dialogues, partnerships, industry forums and market activities.

- Create value through new and enforced commercial models

Is this you?

We believe you are passionate about how technology can create meaningful business outcomes. You combine strategic thinking with a hands-on mindset and enjoy turning opportunities into practical solutions.

You are a strong communicator who can engage with both technical specialists and business stakeholders. You are curious, forward-thinking and motivated by helping others succeed through technology.

Most importantly, you are excited about the possibilities AI creates while remaining pragmatic about how to generate sustainable and long-term value.

What experience you'll likely have

You likely have several years of experience working with technology, business systems, digital transformation or consulting. You have experience leading initiatives and bringing together people, processes and technology to achieve business goals.

We also believe you have:

- Experience driving strategic technology initiatives and business transformation.

- Strong understanding of AI technologies, trends and practical applications.

- Experience working with cloud platforms, data-driven solutions or enterprise software environments.

- The ability to bridge business needs and technical possibilities.

- Experience collaborating with executive stakeholders and cross-functional teams.

We'd be even happier if you also have

- Experience from ERP environments such as IFS, Oracle NetSuite or similar platforms.

- Knowledge of AI governance, responsible AI frameworks and regulatory requirements, including the EU AI Act.

- Experience building AI-powered products, services or advisory offerings.

- Experience working in consulting or customer-facing environments.

This is Addovation

We are a Nordic IT company helping organisations streamline and improve their business processes through innovative business solutions. By combining deep expertise within IFS, Oracle NetSuite and Microsoft technologies, we help our customers create smarter, more efficient ways of working.

Today, Team Addovation consists of more than 200 consultants, specialists and developers across Sweden, Norway and Finland. Together, we create simple and innovative solutions that make a real difference.

Why choose Addovation?

At Addovation, you'll have the opportunity to make a tangible impact in a growing and innovative company. We believe in collaboration, entrepreneurship and continuous learning, and we encourage our employees to influence both their own development and the future direction of our business.

You'll join a company where ideas are welcomed, initiative is valued, and AI is seen as a strategic opportunity to create long-term value for customers and colleagues alike.

How to apply?

If you're excited about helping customers and colleagues unlock the value of AI, we'd love to hear from you. Submit your application through our career page. Applications are reviewed on an ongoing basis.

If you have any questions about the position, please contact our HR Administrator, Seline Schildt, at seline.schildt@addovation.com.

We look forward to your application and the opportunity to get to know you.

title: 05P-Network Services
description:
Who We Are

At Kyndryl, we run and reimagine the mission-critical technology systems that drive advantage for the world’s leading businesses. We are at the heart of progress; with proven expertise and a continuous flow of AI-powered insight, enabling smarter decisions, faster innovation, and a lasting competitive edge. For our people—Kyndryls—that means doing purposeful work that powers human progress. Join us and experience a flexible, supportive environment where your well-being is prioritized and your potential can thrive.


The Role

Do you want to be at the forefront of designing and implementing cutting-edge network solutions? Within our Network Services team at Kyndryl, you will be the go-to expert for providing top-of-the-line technical solutions throughout the entire solution lifecycle. You will be responsible for creating local and wide-area network solutions that utilize multiple platforms and protocols, ensuring that our customers have the best possible network infrastructure to support their business needs. Your skills in routers, networking controllers, bridges, and networking software will be essential as you troubleshoot network issues and coordinate with vendors to install the latest hardware and software, such as routers and switches. Not only will you help keep our customer’s networks running smoothly, but you will also work on project implementation, conduct project planning and cost analysis, and build proof-of-concept solutions with networking system technology. In this role, you will have the opportunity to review project requirements, communicate them accurately to the team, and ensure they are appropriately fulfilled. You will use your expertise to design and implement local and wide-area network solutions, including IP and VOIP, that address customer requirements. You will also provide high-quality technical solutions to our customers to prepare them for implementation, go-live, and maintenance. If you are excited about using your technical expertise to create innovative network solutions and provide outstanding customer service, then this is the role for you! Your Future at Kyndryl At Kyndryl, we understand the importance of investing in our employees' professional growth and development. In Network Services, you can expect to receive a lot of support for training programs to keep your skills and knowledge up to date with the latest industry trends and technologies. By joining our team, you will have the opportunity to work on cutting-edge projects and contribute to the development of innovative solutions for our customers – including new wireless and 5G technologies – not yet adopted by most companies.


Who You Are

You’re good at what you do and possess the required experience to prove it. However, equally as important – you have a growth mindset; keen to drive your own personal and professional development. You are customer-focused – someone who prioritizes customer success in their work. And finally, you’re open and borderless – naturally inclusive in how you work with others. Required Technical and Professional Expertise •6+ years of experience focused on network support, configuration, and implementation •6+ years of experience in core switching, routing, MPLS, and firewalls •Networking and security architecture and engineering support experience across local, regional, and global domains •Ability to effectively execute multiple IT projects and deadlines with limited supervision Preferred Technical and Professional Experience •Application Centric Infrastructure (ACI) deployment and data center experience •Experience with design and implementing Software Defined Network (SDN) and large complex networks •Experience with protocols and technologies such as, BDP, OSPF, MP-FBP EVPN, VXLAN, or VPC


Being You

The “Kyn” in Kyndryl means kinship, which represents the strong bonds we have with each other, our customers and our communities. We focus on ensuring all Kyndryls feel included and we welcome people of all cultures, backgrounds, and experiences. Even if you don’t meet every requirement, we encourage you to apply. We believe in growth, and we’re excited to see what you can bring. At Kyndryl, employee feedback has told us that our number one driver of employee engagement is belonging. That sense of belonging — being a valued, respected, trusted member of the team — is fundamental to our culture and fueling great experiences for our customers. This dedication to welcoming everyone into our company means that Kyndryl gives you the ability to thrive and contribute to our culture of empathy and shared success. That’s The Kyndryl Way.


What You Can Expect

Your career with us isn’t just a job—it’s an adventure with purpose. We offer a dynamic, hybrid-friendly culture that supports your well-being and empowers you to grow. Our Be Well programs are thoughtfully designed to support your financial, mental, physical, and social health—because we know that when you feel your best, you do your best.

From your very first day, you’ll dive into impactful work that powers the systems our customers rely on every day. You won’t just contribute—you’ll make a difference, tackling meaningful projects that sharpen your skills and fuel your growth.

We’re here to champion your journey. With powerful tools to chart your career path, personalized development goals aligned with your ambitions, and continuous feedback to keep you inspired and on track, you’ll have everything you need to thrive and evolve. You’ll develop in-demand skills to grow your career and achieve your ambitions with access to cutting-edge learning opportunities—from certifications with Microsoft, Google, and Amazon to coaching and hands-on experiences. And through it all, you’ll be part of a culture that values empathy, restless learning, and a devotion to shared success.

We want you to thrive here—and we’re committed to helping you do just that. Ready to make an impact? Join us and help shape what’s next.

Get Referred!

If you know someone that works at Kyndryl, when asked ‘How Did You Hear About Us’ during the application process, select ‘Employee Referral’ and enter your contact's Kyndryl email address.

title: Senior Philanthropy Specialist
description:
Love + medicine is who we are, it's what we do, it's why people want to work here. If you’re looking for a job to love, apply today.

Scheduled Weekly Hours:

40

We’re not just filling positions, we’re building careers. At Emplify Health, we care for our teams, while they care for their communities. Whether you are just starting out or looking for a change, Emplify Health supports you now and into the future. Join us and find out how a little empathy changes everything.


Every gift tells a story of hope, compassion, and a desire to make a difference. At Emplify Health, we're looking to hire two Senior Philanthropy Specialists who can inspire that generosity and help donors turn their passion into lasting impact. Through meaningful relationships and strategic partnerships, you'll play a key role in advancing the mission of the Gundersen Medical Foundation and Children's Miracle Network while helping improve the health and well-being of our patients and communities.


The Senior Philanthropy Specialist's primary responsibilities are in the identification, qualification, cultivation, solicitation and stewardship of major and high-capacity prospects and donors of Gundersen Medical Foundation (GMF) and Children's Miracle Network (CMN).

The Senior Philanthropy Specialist will maintain and promote a personal, professional philosophy of community involvement by participating in professional and community activities.


Major Responsibilities Include:

  • Manages a portfolio 100+ high-capacity prospects and legacy donors (individual and corporate), strategically advancing prospects through moves management and successfully closing high-capacity gifts to support GMF/CMN and Emplify by Gundersen.
  • Responsible for developing strategies specifically tailored to individual prospects to move through the solicitation cycle in an efficient and effective manner.
  • Lead donors through complex gifts.
  • Serves as lead for philanthropy specialists and assists with leading and implementing departmental initiatives and process improvements.
  • Partner with executives, physicians, board members and other volunteers.
  • Assist in leading complex donor strategies and campaign priorities.
  • Responsible for meeting established donor/prospect visits, solicitation/proposal and revenue goals.
  • Proactively identify, and formally qualify, new major and planned gift prospects by developing, optimizing and executing long-range and short-term strategies, producing a continuous stream of donors capable of makingmajormaking major gift commitments.
  • Responsible for keeping accurate and timely records of all constituent interaction in CRM.
  • Responsible for preparing personalized correspondence in a timely manner.
  • Provides regular reporting of major gift progress including detailed contact reports of prospective donor visits and submits reports to the Manager of Philanthropy at intervals deemed appropriate by all parties.
  • Responsible for becoming knowledgeable about GMF/GHS and its strategic priorities ot communicate those priorities effectively to donor prospects.
  • Responsible for establishing good working relationships with administration, directors and managers of Emplify Health by Gundersen (GHS) departments and affiliated physicians.
  • Engage Foundation and health system leaders, appropriate providers and volunteers in cultivation and solicitation meetings.
  • Works collaboratively with philanthropy staff to accomplish the goals and objectives of the division.
  • Demonstrates performance, which is consistent with the health system’s mission and values, quality improvement standards, and promotes a culture of patient/family centered care.
  • Elements of performance will include teamwork, innovation, respect, cooperation and honesty to create a positive image across the organization.
  • Keeps abreast of developments in healthcare, the community, business and philanthropy, as well as in the field of prospect research.
  • Maintains own professional growth and development.
  • Complies with all ethical standards as written by The Association of Fundraising Professionals Code of Ethics.
  • Adheres to regular and predictable attendance.
  • Performs other job-related responsibilities as requested.

What's Available:

  • Full time, 1.0 FTE - 40 hours/ week
  • Schedule: Primarily Monday through Friday, daytime business hours ~8:00am-5:00pm. Flexibility is required to support donor meetings, fundraising events, and community engagement activities, which may occasionally include early mornings, evenings, and weekends.
  • Location: Onsite - based in La Crosse, WI.
  • Starting salary of $65,000/year plus more based on relevant work experience



What You'll Need:

  • Education: Bachelor's degree in a health-related field
  • Experience: 1 year of experience in health education or public health in the worksite setting. Preference given for those with experience in point of care testing or use of other health screening equipment.
  • License/ Certification: Valid Driver's License, Required
  • Current Infant-Adult Basic Life Support for Health Care Providers (with hands on learning) from one of the following programs; American Heart Association or American Red Cross within three months of hire - Required
  • Experience conducting biometric screenings and point-of-care testing, preferred
  • Experience utilizing health screening equipment and interpreting screening results, preferred
  • Familiarity with public health principles, health promotion strategies, and community engagement.
  • Comfortable working in a variety of settings, including community events, employer worksites, and healthcare environments.
  • Strong interpersonal and relationship-building skills.
  • Excellent communication and presentation abilities.

In addition to the rewarding work, you'll receive:

  • A highly adaptable and mission-driven organization with a work environment that supports you personally and professionally and a work culture where you are valued and appreciated
  • Competitive Benefits: A comprehensive and generous benefits package (Medical, Dental, Life Ins, HSA/FSA) ensuring your comfort and well-being as a valuable team member
  • Substantial retirement contribution including a 401k match & annual discretionary base contribution
  • Work-Life Balance: Paid Time Off (PTO) combines vacation, sick, and personal days into one balance to allow you the flexibility to use your time off as you need
  • Professional Development: Support for your career growth through Professional Development Opportunities, our Tuition Investment Program, and our Career Development Center
  • Additional Employee Discounts and Perks Other benefits include a Wellness program with incentives, employer-paid life insurance and AD&D, optional short-term and long-term disability coverage, an employee assistance program, identity theft protection, pet insurance, Inspire & Celebrate colleague recognition and rewards program, a discount program, and more!

PRACTICES AND PROMOTES BEHAVIOR CONSISTENT WITH THE MISSION, VISION AND VALUES:


Mission:

Together, we inspire your best life by relentlessly caring, learning and innovating.

Vision:

Leading with love, we courageously commit to a future of healthy people and thriving communities.

Values:

Belonging, Respect, Excellence, Accountability, Teamwork, Humility


Emplify Health is comprised of two of the Midwest’s most respected healthcare systems, Bellin Health and Gundersen Health System. Once neighbors, we are now partners, united in our mission to provide exceptional care to our communities. As a not-for-profit, patient-centered healthcare network, we have headquarters in Green Bay and La Crosse, Wisconsin. Our extensive network includes 11 hospitals and more than 100 clinics, serving 67 cities and rural communities across Wisconsin, Iowa, Minnesota and Michigan’s Upper Peninsula. With over 4,500 dedicated nurses and providers, we are committed to delivering primary, specialty and emergency care, along with innovative medical education programs. Join us in making a meaningful difference in the lives of our patients and communities


If you need assistance with any portion of the application or have questions about the position, please contact HR-Recruitment@gundersenhealth.org or call 608-775-0267.

We inspire your best life by relentlessly caring, learning and innovating. This is our purpose. Together with our values — belonging, respect, excellence, accountability, teamwork and humility — our pillars set our foundation and our future.

Equal Opportunity Employer

title: Data & AI Apprenticeship - Edinburgh
description:
Please note, this site is only for external candidate applications. If you currently work for Lloyds Banking Group please apply via the internal career site.

Please note: In order to complete an apprenticeship there needs to be a significant learning need. You need to consider your previous qualifications or significant relevant work experience which may mean you cannot proceed with this application.

End Date

We support flexible working – click here for more information on flexible working options

Flexible Working Options

Hybrid Working

Job Description Summary

Prior to submitting your application, please visit our early careers website to find out more about the programmes we offer and the recruitment journey: www.lloydsbankinggrouptalent.com.

Our apprenticeship programmes may close early if we receive a high number of applications, so it’s best to apply as soon as you can.

If you have any questions, please do contact the team at lloydsbankinggroup@cappfinity.com


Job Description

Salary : £27,400
Location: Edinburgh

Start: September 2027
Qualification: Level 4 Data Analyst Apprenticeship with BPP. Successfully complete that and you’ll move on to a level 6 Degree Apprenticeship in Data Science or Digital Technology Solutions.

Your data journey starts here. Show us what you’re made of

At Lloyds Banking Group, data isn’t just numbers on a screen. It’s the fuel for every decision we make, every problem we solve, every idea that takes us forward.

We’re the UK’s biggest digital bank, with 23 million customers logging in, tapping and scrolling every day. And with £3bn a year going into cloud, AI and analytics, we’re serious about data shaping the future.

As a Data Apprentice, you’ll learn how to tame big, messy datasets, spot patterns no one else can see, and turn them into insights that make banking smarter, safer and simpler.

Three to four years. Two apprenticeships. Unlimited potential

This isn’t just one programme - it’s your first step to an amazing career. You’ll begin with a level 4 Applied Data and AI Specialist apprenticeship. Do well, and successfully complete this, and you’ll move on to a level 6 degree apprenticeship, deepening your skills while growing your career with us.

Along the way, you’ll dive into:

  • SQL and advanced data joins (yes, the fun kind)
  • Predictive modelling & forecasting (basically, time travel with stats)
  • Data visualisation & storytelling (making numbers talk)
  • Analytics lifecycles & data democratisation
  • Statistical programming languages
  • Building data products people actually use

By the end, you won’t just know data. You’ll live and breathe data.

The impact you could make

  • Spot patterns that stop fraud before it happens
  • Help millions of customers make smarter money choices
  • Build dashboards that leaders can’t live without
  • Make data accessible, ethical and useful for everyone

Your skills toolkit

You’ll master:

  • SQL, Python and other stats superpowers
  • Visualisation that makes people go “ohhh, now I get it”
  • Forecasting and modelling
  • AI literacy and applied analytics
  • Turning complexity into clarity

Support in your corner

We’ll set you up to shine with:

  • Blended learning: real projects + classroom theory
  • Time carved out just for your development
  • A mentor, a manager and a buddy (because no one should debug alone)
  • A community that shares your passion and goals

Your future. Fully funded

We’ll cover your salary and fully fund your qualifications, setting you up for success with a level 4 apprenticeship in Applied Data and AI. You’ll gain hands-on experience working with some of the UK’s largest and most complex datasets, develop versatile skills that open doors across analytics and AI, and have the opportunity to progress to a Level 6 Degree Apprenticeship equipping you to grow from a specialist into a strategist.

Requirements

What you need to apply

  • You’ll need to be at least 18 years old by the end of February 2028
  • National 5 Maths & English at grades A-C (Achieved)
  • 4 Highers BBCC (these grades can be predicted, but any offer made to you will be conditional upon successful achievement of these qualifications)

Important information

An additional requirement for the apprenticeship position is that you must currently possess a valid Right to Work in the UK. Your visa end date must extend beyond the duration of the apprenticeship programme, which will last up to five years.

Due to Home Office requirements regarding Skilled Workers, we’re unable to accept applications for visa sponsorship for our apprenticeship roles as the proposed salary for the role does not meet the minimum threshold – if this situation applies to you, please consider looking for other vacancies which may be more suitable.

Location

This apprenticeship is based in Edinburgh, and you will be expected to work from your primary office location throughout the programme. While our hybrid working policy requires office attendance at least two days per week (40% for full-time colleagues), apprentices are expected to be in the office most days during the initial settling-in period.

If your commute exceeds 1.5 hours, we strongly recommend relocating closer to the office to ensure consistent attendance in line with contractual and hybrid working expectations.

About working for us
Our ambition is to be the leading UK business for diversity, equity and inclusion supporting our customers, colleagues and communities and we’re committed to creating an environment in which everyone can thrive, learn and develop.

We were one of the first major organisations to set goals on diversity in senior roles, create a menopause health package, and a dedicated Working with Cancer Initiative.

We offer reasonable workplace adjustments for colleagues with disabilities, including flexibility in office attendance, location and working patterns. And, as a Disability Confident Leader, we guarantee interviews for a fair and proportionate number of applicants who meet the minimum criteria for the role with a disability, long-term health or neurodivergent condition through the Disability Confident Scheme.

We provide reasonable adjustments throughout the recruitment process to reduce or remove barriers. Just let us know what you need.

Salary

You will join us on a fixed apprenticeship salary. Upon successful completion of the apprenticeship, you will be re-graded, with your pay range consistent with the job family for your business area.

We also offer a wide-ranging benefits package, which includes:

  • A generous pension contribution of up to 15%
  • An annual performance-related bonus
  • Share schemes including free shares
  • Benefits you can adapt to your lifestyle, such as discounted shopping
  • 22 days’ holiday, with bank holidays on top
  • A range of wellbeing initiatives and generous parental leave policies

The closing date to apply for this opportunity is 12th January.

Our roles generate a lot of interest and occasionally we need to close for applications earlier than originally advertised. If you think working with us could be right for you, please apply now and see where an apprenticeship with us can take you!

title: Senior Manager, Software Engineering (Observability, Kafka, Monitoring)
description:
To get the best candidate experience, please consider applying for a maximum of 3 roles within 12 months to ensure you are not duplicating efforts.

Job Category

Software Engineering

Job Details

About Salesforce

Salesforce is the #1 AI CRM, where humans with agents drive customer success together. Here, ambition meets action. Tech meets trust. And innovation isn’t a buzzword — it’s a way of life. The world of work as we know it is changing and we're looking for Trailblazers who are passionate about bettering business and the world through AI, driving innovation, and keeping Salesforce's core values at the heart of it all.

Ready to level-up your career at the company leading workforce transformation in the agentic era? You’re in the right place! Agentforce is the future of AI, and you are the future of Salesforce.

The Experience

You will be a Senior Manager of Software Engineering leading a team of 8 to 10 engineers. Your team builds the “Anomaly Alerting” platform. This is a smart system that watches for strange changes in data and sends out warnings. Your job is to guide the people, own the system, and help make our warning alerts smarter and more automatic.

What You’ll Actually Be Doing

  • Day-to-day work: You will make sure our alerting system is fast, strong, and does not break as it grows. You will lead projects that make the system do the hard work so other teams don’t have to set up alerts by hand.
  • Leading the way: You will manage 1 to 2 teams (8 to 10 engineers). You will build a happy, helpful culture where people work well together.
  • Working together: You will partner with other tech teams and groups across Salesforce (like Slack and Sales Cloud) so they can find and fix problems much faster. You will also speak for your team in meetings and work closely with our teams in the US.
  • Early goals & impact: In your first 60 to 90 days, you will learn the ropes, start leading in meetings, team up with the US groups, and make a real difference on our biggest goals.



You’re Our Person If...

  • You have experience being a manager and leading 8 to 10 software engineers.
  • You know how to handle huge amounts of data and build data pipelines (ETL).
  • You have experience running systems on big clouds like AWS or Google Cloud (GCP).
  • You have worked with tools that monitor system health (Observability).
  • You have some experience with Machine Learning and know how to spot strange patterns in data (Anomaly Detection).
  • You are able to work in the office as the company requires (no travel is required for this role).



Even Better If...

  • You have deep, hands-on experience building Machine Learning tools that send out alerts.
  • You already know how to work with Salesforce products like Agentforce, Commerce Cloud, or Slack.



Tech Stack:

  • Cloud & Compute: AWS, GCP, and Kubernetes (EKS/GKE) for stateless, scalable multi-cloud orchestration.
  • Infrastructure as Code: Terraform for resilient, automated platform provisioning across environments.
  • Edge Ingestion: OpenTelemetry (OTel) for standardized instrumentation, and Vector/Fluent Bit for high-throughput log routing.
  • Message Buffering: Apache Kafka to ingest billions of telemetry events, ensuring durable, decoupled data pipelines.
  • Stream Processing: Apache Flink for real-time log parsing, rolling aggregations, and anomaly detection before storage.
  • Backend Languages: Java for building heavy stream-processing applications, supplemented by Go and Python for operators and tooling.
  • Ad-Hoc OLAP Analytics: Apache Druid to power sub-second, interactive dashboard queries over massive historical datasets.
  • Log & Trace Storage: ClickHouse for fast columnar event storage, natively tiered to AWS S3 / GCP Cloud Storage for cost-effective cold storage.
  • Time-Series Metrics: VictoriaMetrics, M3DB, or Prometheus to ingest and compress millions of high-cardinality metric rollups.
  • Visualization & Alerting: Grafana and Apache Superset for single-pane-of-glass UI, paired with Prometheus Alertmanager for incident routing.
  • A demonstrated, genuine AI-first approach to engineering — using AI to move faster, build fluency across the stack, and contribute well beyond your core specialty.
  • Experience using AI tools (e.g., Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Codex, Cursor, etc.) in development workflows.
  • Advanced prompt engineering skills and the ability to write precise, structured prompts and cultivate the system context that makes AI outputs reliable, secure, and production-ready.

Unleash Your Potential

When you join Salesforce, you’ll be limitless in all areas of your life. Our benefits and resources support you to find balance and be your best, and our AI agents accelerate your impact so you can do your best. Together, we’ll bring the power of Agentforce to organizations of all sizes and deliver amazing experiences that customers love. Apply today to not only shape the future — but to redefine what’s possible — for yourself, for AI, and the world.

Accommodations

If you need a reasonable accommodation during the application or the recruiting process, please submit a request via this Accommodations Request Form.

Please note that Salesforce uses artificial intelligence (AI) tools to help our recruiters assess and evaluate candidates’ resumes and qualifications throughout the recruiting process. Humans will always make any candidate selection and hiring decisions. Please see our Candidate Privacy Statement for more information about how we use your personal data and your rights, including with regard to use of AI tools and opt out options.

Posting Statement

Salesforce is an equal opportunity employer and maintains a policy of non-discrimination with all employees and applicants for employment. What does that mean exactly? It means that at Salesforce, we believe in equality for all. And we believe we can lead the path to equality in part by creating a workplace that’s inclusive, and free from discrimination. Know your rights: workplace discrimination is illegal. Any employee or potential employee will be assessed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications – without regard to race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender expression or identity, transgender status, age, disability, veteran or marital status, political viewpoint, or other classifications protected by law. This policy applies to current and prospective employees, no matter where they are in their Salesforce employment journey. It also applies to recruiting, hiring, job assignment, compensation, promotion, benefits, training, assessment of job performance, discipline, termination, and everything in between. title: Global Service Manager AMS – AI Ops and CSI
description:
Job Description Summary

Sandoz continues to go through an exciting and transformative period as a global leader and pioneering provider of sustainable Biosimilar and Generic medicines. As we continue down this new and ambitious path, unique opportunities will present themselves, both professionally and personally. Join us, the future is ours to shape!

As the Global Service Manager, AI Ops and CSI, you will be responsible for driving proactive, data-driven Application Management Services (AMS) operations through AI-powered service management, automation and continuous improvement initiatives. The role partners closely with business stakeholders, application owners, infrastructure teams and AMS providers to improve service quality, operational efficiency and user experience across the global application landscape.

Job Description

Your Key Responsibilities:


Lead AI Ops and Continual Service Improvement (CSI) across the global AMS portfolio to enable proactive, data-driven operations, intelligent automation and measurable improvements in service quality, efficiency and user experience.


  • Own the AI Ops and CSI strategy, operating framework and governance cadence across in-scope applications and AMS providers; define priorities, decision rights, delivery standards and escalation routes aligned to business needs and approved service commitments.
  • Build and govern a prioritised AI Ops use-case pipeline covering anomaly detection, event correlation, alert-noise reduction, incident classification and routing, knowledge recommendations and assisted root-cause analysis; assess data readiness, feasibility, expected value and delivery effort before progressing from pilot to scale.
  • Coordinate application owners, EAS, Infrastructure and AMS providers to establish actionable observability across application logs, metrics, events and service dependencies; govern data quality, contextual enrichment and integration with monitoring, ITSM and configuration records to support reliable operational insights.
  • Drive proactive incident and problem management through AI-assisted triage, impact assessment, trend analysis and identification of recurring issues; ensure insights translate into owned corrective actions, improved knowledge articles and permanent fixes, with operational teams validating recommendations before execution.
  • Govern intelligent automation for repetitive support activities, service requests, diagnostics and approved remediation runbooks; require clear ownership, access controls, testing, exception handling, human approval where appropriate and change-controlled deployment, and measure reductions in manual effort and processing time.
  • Own a consolidated CSI register and rolling improvement roadmap, drawing on service reviews, incident and problem trends, SLA performance, user feedback and delivery bottlenecks; define each initiative’s problem statement, baseline, target outcome, accountable owner, milestones, dependencies and acceptance criteria.
  • Lead cross-functional improvement delivery with business stakeholders, application owners, EAS, Infrastructure, Quality and AMS providers; remove process hand-off gaps, standardise support practices, manage dependencies and escalate overdue actions, while keeping initiatives within approved capacity and commercial scope.
  • Establish baselines and dashboards for incident recurrence, mean time to detect and resolve, alert quality, automation adoption, request turnaround, SLA attainment and user experience; validate realised benefits against agreed measures, distinguish released capacity from cash savings and use results to reprioritise the roadmap.
  • Maintain clear accountability boundaries: this role governs the AMS AI Ops and CSI roadmap, outcomes and provider commitments; application owners approve application-specific requirements and acceptance; platform teams own enabling technology; AMS providers implement and operate approved capabilities; designated governance and Quality functions approve applicable controls.

Key performance indicators:


  • AI Ops adoption and coverage: proportion of prioritised use cases deployed and actively used, and in-scope applications with actionable observability and validated operational data, measured against agreed roadmap targets.
  • Alert quality and incident response: reduction in duplicate and non-actionable alerts, improved incident classification and routing accuracy, and reduced mean time to detect and resolve incidents against agreed service baselines.
  • Automation effectiveness: proportion of eligible support activities automated, successful execution rate, reduction in manual effort and request turnaround time, and exception rates within agreed thresholds for approved workflows.
  • Recurring-incident reduction: decrease in repeat incidents for prioritised problem areas, timely closure of root-cause corrective actions and sustained effectiveness of permanent fixes against agreed baseline and review periods.
  • CSI roadmap delivery: proportion of prioritised initiatives completed on time and accepted against agreed outcomes, with current baselines, accountable owners and benefits measures; reduction in overdue milestones and improvement actions.
  • Realised service and business benefits: validated improvements in SLA attainment and user satisfaction, released support capacity and cost efficiency against agreed baselines and targets, with released capacity reported separately from realised cash savings.

Minimum Requirements:
Education


Degree in IT, Computer Science, Engineering, Data Science or equivalent; ITIL Foundation required. Advanced certification in IT service management, continual improvement, AI Ops, data analytics, automation or cloud operations desirable.


Languages

Fluent written and spoken English.


Experience & Skills


  • 10+ years in IT, including 5+ years in application service management, operational improvement, intelligent automation or regulated managed-service delivery, with practical experience applying AI Ops and CSI.
  • Proven global, multi-supplier governance of AI Ops use cases and CSI roadmaps, including prioritisation, baseline definition, delivery oversight, adoption and measurable benefits realisation.
  • Strong ITIL incident, problem, change, release, service-level and continual-improvement knowledge; experience with ServiceNow, CMDB, observability, event-management and automation platforms.
  • Strong analytical judgement, supplier management, improvement facilitation, change adoption, executive communication and cross-functional leadership; ability to translate operational insights into prioritised actions and demonstrate improvements in service quality, efficiency and user experience.

Skills Desired

Agile Project Management, Business Partnering, Change Management, IT Service Delivery, Performance Management

title: Field Service Site Supervisor
description:
Field Service Site Supervisor – Germany


At JBT Marel, we are looking for a Field Service Site Supervisor based in Germany to oversee equipment installations, start-up activities and preventive maintenance agreements at customer sites around the world.

This is an international, hands-on role for someone with a strong electrical background, a practical mindset and the confidence to work independently. You will coordinate local contractors and customer crews, take ownership of complex site challenges and ensure projects are delivered safely, efficiently and to the required standards.

The role involves global travel for approximately 160–210 days per year, with assignments typically lasting between 2 and 8 weeks away from home.


What You'll Be Doing

  • Supervising equipment installations, start-up activities and preventive maintenance agreements at customer sites worldwide.
  • Coordinating and overseeing field service engineers, local contractors and customer crews to ensure work is completed safely and efficiently.
  • Ensuring compliance with safety, quality and regulatory standards throughout project execution.
  • Conducting pre-installation site visits to verify site layouts, technical requirements and customer readiness.
  • Managing schedules, resources and priorities while independently resolving complex technical and logistical challenges.
  • Communicating project progress, issues and requirements to customers, project management and internal stakeholders, preparing reports and documenting lessons learned.
  • Providing technical guidance to less experienced colleagues, supporting their development and contributing to continuous improvement and customer satisfaction.

Experience & Education

  • A strong electrical background is essential, supported by in-depth knowledge of electrical systems and a basic understanding of related technical disciplines.
  • Experience in field service, site supervision, equipment installation, commissioning, maintenance engineering or a similar technical role.
  • Experience coordinating contractors, customer teams or technical personnel on-site.
  • The ability to troubleshoot complex problems, make sound decisions and work independently with minimal guidance.
  • Experience leading project activities, supporting less experienced colleagues and contributing to process improvements.
  • Excellent written and verbal English is mandatory.
  • Willingness and ability to travel globally for 160–210 days per year, including assignments of 2–8 weeks away from home.
  • Previous experience in the food processing or industrial machinery sector would be advantageous.

Working Style

Your mentality is the most important factor. We are looking for someone who is proactive, resilient, dependable and solution-focused. You should be comfortable working alone for extended periods, taking ownership of challenges and adapting to different customers, cultures and working environments.


Who Are We?

We are the kind of people who find purpose in creating things. Our mission is to transform the future of food by creating a world where quality food is produced sustainably and affordably.


At JBT Marel, we are uniquely positioned to make this happen. By combining technology, innovation and expertise, we help food producers around the world improve efficiency, productivity and sustainability.

If you are passionate about Excellence, Innovation and Unity, we invite you to join our global team and help us shape the future of food.


Interested?


If you have the electrical expertise, independent mindset and willingness to travel internationally, we'd love to hear from you.

Visit to learn more about us and explore your future with JBT Marel.

title: Senior Manager, Medical Affairs, LATAM
description:
What if the work you did every day could impact the lives of people you know? Or all of humanity?

At Illumina, we are expanding access to genomic technology to realize health equity for billions of people around the world. Our efforts enable life-changing discoveries that are transforming human health through the early detection and diagnosis of diseases and new treatment options for patients.

Working at Illumina means being part of something bigger than yourself. Every person, in every role, has the opportunity to make a difference. Surrounded by extraordinary people, inspiring leaders, and world changing projects, you will do more and become more than you ever thought possible.

Senior Manager, Medical Affairs, LATAM

Location - Sao Paulo, Brazil


As Senior Manager, Medical Affairs, LATAM at Illumina, you will help shape and deliver our Medical Affairs strategy across Latin America, with primary responsibility for Brazil. You will translate regional and global priorities into practical plans that advance clinical evidence generation, scientific engagement, and healthcare professional education across oncology, reproductive health, rare and inherited diseases, infectious diseases, and emerging clinical applications. The role includes day-to-day guidance and oversight for a regional Medical Affairs colleague supporting Spanish-speaking Latin America.

Why you


You combine scientific credibility with the ability to turn strategy into action. You can lead through influence in a matrixed environment, build trusted relationships with external scientific stakeholders, and balance regional priorities across different markets and healthcare systems. You are comfortable moving between strategic planning and hands-on execution, and you bring the judgement required to support compliant, evidence-based scientific exchange.


Responsibilities include

  • Drive implementation of the Medical Affairs strategy for Latin America in alignment with regional and global priorities.
  • Lead Medical Affairs activities in Brazil and provide guidance to the Medical Affairs colleague covering Spanish-speaking Latin America.
  • Coordinate regional initiatives across clinical evidence generation, scientific engagement, and medical education.
  • Identify and qualify opportunities for investigator collaborations, clinical evidence generation, and healthcare professional education.
  • Build and maintain relationships with key opinion leaders, healthcare institutions, academic centers, and professional societies.
  • Support investigator-initiated studies, collaborative research, real-world evidence programs, and educational activities.
  • Partner with R&D and global Medical Affairs to provide scientific insights relevant to Latin American markets.
  • Collaborate with Account Management, Marketing, Market Access, Government Affairs, Customer Support, Regulatory, and other teams to support clinical implementation and adoption of Illumina technologies.
  • Contribute to scientific communications, publications, congress activities, advisory boards, and educational materials.
  • Provide regional scientific input into business planning and translate customer and market insights into actionable recommendations.
  • Monitor scientific, clinical, competitive, and healthcare policy developments across Latin America.
  • Ensure Medical Affairs activities comply with applicable regulatory, privacy, ethical, and company requirements.

Preferred background, skills and experience

  • Solid Medical Affairs experience within diagnostics, genomics, biotechnology, pharmaceuticals, life sciences, or a related healthcare field.
  • Strong scientific knowledge of molecular diagnostics, genomics, precision medicine, or related fields.
  • Experience supporting clinical evidence generation, scientific engagement, healthcare professional education, or clinical implementation initiatives.
  • Experience leading regional or cross-functional initiatives and providing guidance to colleagues in a matrixed organization.
  • Experience working across multiple countries or diverse healthcare systems is preferred.
  • Experience engaging key opinion leaders, healthcare providers, academic institutions, and cross-functional partners.
  • Strong stakeholder management, communication, and influencing skills.
  • Fluency in English and Portuguese; Spanish proficiency is strongly preferred.
  • Ability to travel approximately 50-70% across Latin America and internationally.

Preferred education and experience

  • PhD, MD, PharmD, MSc, or equivalent advanced degree in Life Sciences, Genetics, Molecular Biology, Medicine, Biomedical Sciences, or a related field is preferred.
  • Extensive, relevant experience in Medical Affairs, clinical research, molecular diagnostics, genomics, biotechnology, or a related healthcare field. Advanced degrees may be considered toward relevant experience.
  • Previous formal people management experience is preferred, demonstrated leadership in matrix or project-based environments may substitute for formal management experience.

title: Editor-in-Chief, The Lancet Psychiatry
description:
In-house Editor-in-Chief


Do you enjoy using science to drive change in the world?


Ready to shape the future of mental health, science and practice?


Location: London

About our Team


The Lancet Psychiatry, an established monthly print and online hybrid journal, seeks an in-house Editor-in Chief. The Lancet Psychiatry was launched in June 2014 with the aim “to play a pivotal role in disseminating new findings and fostering debate that enables clinicians and policy makers to improve the lives of people with mental health problems”. The new Editor-in Chief must be a subject expert who can continue this mission via the publication of high-impact, practice-changing research, review, and provocative comment and opinion in mental health, providing a clear, independent perspective about the clinical advances and cutting-edge research shaping mental health globally.


About the Role


As an in-house Editor-in-Chief, you are a subject expert who will oversee the assessment and publication of original material for our journal. You will take ownership of submissions and oversee rigorous in-depth peer review to ensure we publish high-quality content. You will build global networks with experts in the community, including experts with lived experience of mental illness, to attract and disseminate the highest quality work from the field.

At the Lancet, we are deeply committed to fostering a diverse, equitable, and inclusive environment. In our pursuit of excellence, we recognise the strength in varied perspectives, experiences, and backgrounds. As part of our ongoing efforts to enhance the diversity of our editorial team, we encourage applications from individuals who bring unique skills, backgrounds, and perspectives to the role.


Responsibilities


  • Managing the day-to-day editorial handling of papers and peer-review and drive the editorial strategy of The Lancet Psychiatry
  • Direct line management of a Deputy and Senior Editor
  • Developing and maintaining relationships with the mental health community globally to source high-quality, practice-changing research for the journal
  • Commissioning material including Comments, Reviews, Personal Views, Health Policy, and Commissions
  • Attending conferences and events to represent the journal, keeping up to date with current developments in mental health and identifying topics of interest
  • Writing editorials and other content for the journal as required
  • Helping devise new initiatives for future development of the journal
  • Participate in projects across The Lancet Group and, on occasion, with Elsevier and RELX

Requirements


  • A Medical Degree in a relevant discipline or a PhD in a related subject field with postdoctoral research experience
  • Extensive editorial experience, at Editor or other senior level, with a good understanding of all aspects of the editorial process, journal production, and of running an editorial team
  • Be able to demonstrate thorough knowledge of biological and medical sciences, and broader social issues pertaining to mental health. Ability to maintain a balanced, evidence-driven approach in managing controversial areas of the field
  • The ability to engage, influence, and build relationships with external stakeholders, including medical and research professionals, people with lived experience of mental illness, and a range of internal teams
  • Excellent organisational skills and the ability to work efficiently to demanding press deadlines
  • Excellent command of the English language and the ability to write in an engaging and interesting manner
  • Proficient with IT systems including MS Office

Work in a way that works for you


We promote a healthy work/life balance across the organisation. With an average length of service of 9 years, we are confident that we offer an appealing working prospect for our people. With numerous wellbeing initiatives, family leave, and tuition reimbursement, we will help you meet both your immediate responsibilities and long-term goals.


  • Working remotely from home and at our office in a hybrid working style
  • Working flexible hours - flexing the times you work in the day

title: Plasma and Laser Physics Engineer
description:
Introduction to the job

The EUV Source team in San Diego operates in a fast-paced, innovative, and highly technical environment to deliver next-generation products that support the commercialization of Extreme Ultraviolet (EUV) lithography technology.

As a Plasma and Laser Physics Engineer within the EUV Source Performance team, you will play a critical role in validating and optimizing EUV source performance to ensure products meet or exceed customer requirements and expectations.

You will contribute throughout the product development lifecycle by participating in technology development, system validation, performance improvement initiatives, and customer support activities. This role combines advanced physics, data analysis, experimental design, and hands-on engineering to solve complex technical challenges and enable world-class system performance.

Role and responsibilities

As a Plasma and Laser Physics Engineer, you will:

  • Develop system-level expertise on EUV light source performance, including laser generation and amplification, laser-plasma interactions, debris mitigation, and control systems.
  • Apply theoretical models, scientific methods, and experimental techniques to analyze source performance across multiple technical disciplines.
  • Design, execute, and document scientific experiments to validate and optimize prototype hardware and software performance.
  • Develop and execute system and subsystem test plans, ensuring traceability of system requirements.
  • Collect, process, and analyze large datasets using MATLAB, Python, and automated diagnostic tools.
  • Troubleshoot complex performance issues, perform root-cause analysis, and recommend corrective actions and design improvements.
  • Use advanced diagnostic equipment and analytical tools to characterize and validate system performance.
  • Create clear technical documentation, communicate findings, and align recommendations with cross-functional stakeholders.
  • Collaborate closely with system architects, design engineers, scientists, manufacturing teams, customer support engineers, and senior leadership.
  • Support customer escalations through remote and on-site troubleshooting, data analysis, and system recovery activities.
  • Provide technical training and knowledge transfer to factory and field engineering teams.
  • Travel as needed to support customer-site troubleshooting and performance recovery efforts.
  • Ensure safe operation of equipment and adherence to ASML safety procedures.
  • Other duties as assigned.

Education and experience

To help us solve some of the semiconductor industry's most challenging technical problems, you'll need a strong background in plasma physics, optics, and complex system development. You'll need:

  • Bachelor's degree in Plasma Physics, Engineering Physics, Applied Physics, or a related field. Master's or PhD preferred.
  • Must possess 5 years of related experience.
  • Experience with optics, laser-induced plasma, optical metrology, and/or control systems.
  • Experience working with complex system integration and multidisciplinary engineering environments.
  • Experience designing and executing scientific experiments for product development and validation.
  • Proficiency with MATLAB, Python, or similar data analysis and modeling tools
  • Experience with semiconductor equipment development is preferred.
  • Hands-on experience operating optical, electrical, or plasma-related laboratory instrumentation is a plus.

Skills

Working at the forefront of semiconductor technology means solving complex challenges alongside a diverse team of scientists and engineers. Success in this role requires a combination of technical expertise, analytical thinking, and strong collaboration skills.

To thrive in this job, you'll need the following skills:

  • Strong understanding of optics, lasers, plasma generation, and control systems.
  • Excellent analytical, troubleshooting, and root-cause analysis capabilities.
  • Ability to translate technical requirements into comprehensive test plans and procedures.
  • Ability to interpret and summarize large datasets and effectively communicate results through reports and visualizations.
  • Strong laboratory and experimental skills, including operation of test and analytical equipment.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Strong interpersonal and relationship-building skills across cross-functional teams.
  • Ability to create clear technical documentation, procedures, and work instructions.
  • Self-directed with the ability to execute technical tasks with minimal supervision.
  • Customer-focused mindset with the ability to support high-priority field escalations and technical recovery efforts.
  • Demonstrated ability to work effectively in a dynamic, fast-paced, and highly collaborative environment.

Other Information

  • This position is located on-site in San Diego, CA . It requires onsite presence to attend in-person work-related events, trainings and meetings and to further ensure teamwork, collaboration and innovation.
  • A flexible workplace arrangement may be available to employees working in roles conducive to remote work (up to two days a week).
  • Routinely required to sit; walk; talk; hear; use hands to keyboard, finger, handle, and feel; stoop, kneel, crouch, twist, reach, and stretch. Occasionally required to move around the campus.
  • Occasionally lift and/or move up to 20 pounds.
  • Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and ability to adjust focus.
  • Must be willing to work in a clean room environment, wearing coveralls, hoods, booties, safety glasses and gloves for entire duration of shift.
  • While performing the duties of this job, the employee routinely is required to sit; walk; talk; hear; use hands to keyboard, finger, handle, and feel; stoop, kneel, crouch, twist, reach, and stretch.

  • Degree in Mathematics (i.e., Applied Math, Engineering, etc), Statistics, Computer Science, Life Science, or equivalent experience

  • Ability to develop individuals
  • Ability to manage risk in complicated or novel situations

  • Project mentality

Here your decisions carry weight and your expertise is visible. We combine scientific rigor with a mindset of continuous improvement, investing in advanced tools and data capabilities so you can push the craft of programming forward. We value kindness alongside ambition, encourage constructive challenge, and learn openly from setbacks—because that is how we find better paths and create impact that lasts.

Step into a high-exposure leadership role where your programming expertise shapes pivotal trials and advances patient health—take the lead on what’s next today!

When we put unexpected teams in the same room, we unleash bold thinking with the power to inspire life-changing medicines. title: Retail Store Management - New Store
description:
Position Overview

If you are interested in growing your retail management career with one of the largest and fastest growing off-price retailers in the nation, join the Burlington Stores team as a Store Manager! Are you a proven leader with strong communication and organization skills? Can you lead a team in driving results while building strong teams and partnerships and cultivating an environment based on trust, respect, and integrity? Can you bring innovative ideas to help drive results as you take on the challenge of running all aspects of a multi-million-dollar store operation? If you answer yes, then this may be the right opportunity for you.

As a Store Manager, you’ll be responsible for successfully managing all store operations tasks to maximize sales results while bringing “Our Burlington” values to life in your store. You will be a mentor, role model, and coach for your team members, as well as a partner to associates in other branches of the organization. You will lead your team by example, demonstrating how to deliver excellent customer service with a high degree of professionalism and provide a world-class shopping experience to customers. You will take ownership for the successful execution of all day-to-day merchandising, operations and service management tasks. You are ultimately responsible for the overall success of your store location and the associates on your team.

A Day in the Life

  • Direct management and oversight of Assistant Managers, Supervisors, and Store Associates to ensure implementation of established company policies, standards, expectations and initiatives.
  • Ensure Assistant Managers and store team members are fulfilling their individual responsibilities.
  • Partner with Assistant Store Manager, Merchandising to coordinate merchandise placement, sales promotions and pricing.
  • Partner with Assistant Store Manager, Operations to review receiving, transfers, debits/damages, returns-to-vendor (RTV's), and chargeback paperwork to ensure accuracy of inventory.
  • Act as Manager on Duty (MOD); lead by example, set the standard, and create a strong leadership presence by following and modeling the Burlington SOPs.
  • Manage multi-million-dollar sales volume and expense budget including review of all associated reporting and record-keeping.
  • Recruitment, screening and hiring of associates in order to meet store staffing needs.
  • Facilitate onboarding and training for new associates, provide ongoing coaching in the moment, and implement structured learning and development activities for all team members.
  • Handle personnel and associate relations issues.
  • Payroll budget management, workforce management and scheduling.
  • Facilitate effective communication and partnerships among the store team, district and regional management teams, and other partners within the company.

You'll Come With

  • 5+ years of Retail Management experience in a Big Box or Specialty environment
  • Must be able to work a flexible schedule; including early mornings, nights, weekends, and holidays as required.
  • Ability to lift and move boxes weighing up to 40 lbs.
  • Experience utilizing scheduling and reporting computer software
  • Travel may be required from time to time.

Pay Range

  • Store Manager: $78,140 - $97,675 / annual
  • Operations/Service Manager: $24.35 - $32.45 / hour

Come join our team. You’re going to like it here!

You will enjoy a competitive wage, flexible hours, and an associate discount. Burlington’s benefits package includes medical, dental and vision coverage including life and disability insurance. Full time associates may also be eligible for up to 12 days of paid time off annually, up to 8 paid holidays, paid sick time in accordance with applicable law, and a 401(k) plan. We are a rapidly growing brand and provide a variety of training and development opportunities so our associates can grow with us.

Our store teams work hard and have fun together! Burlington associates make a difference in the lives of customers, colleagues, and the communities where we live and work every day. Burlington Stores, Inc. is an equal opportunity employer committed to workplace diversity.

Individual pay decisions will be based on a variety of factors, such as but not limited to, qualifications, education, job-related skills, relevant experience, and geographic location.

description:
